messages.text: Has Verstappen feud reignited at wrong time for Russell?

metadata.summary: The reignition of the long-running feud between George Russell and Max Verstappen has added an entertaining twist to the end of the 2026 Formula 1 season, but it may not be what the Mercedes driver needed at this moment.
metadata.content: Max Verstappen and George Russell: Has feud reignited at wrong time for Mercedes driver after difficult 2026 F1 season? | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Max Verstappen and George Russell: Has feud reignited at wrong time for Mercedes driver after difficult 2026 F1 season? The feud between George Russell and Max Verstappen reignited in spectacular style in Las Vegas following a clash between the pair in practice; watch the Qatar Grand Prix live on Sky Sports this weekend, with qualifying at 6pm on Saturday and the race at 4pm on Sunday Monday 23 November 2026 18:44, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A look back at some of the most heated clashes between Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Mercedes' George Russell The reignition of the long-running feud between George Russell and Max Verstappen has added an entertaining twist to the end of the 2026 Formula 1 season, but it may not be what the Mercedes driver needed at this moment. Russell and Verstappen clashed during final practice at the Las Vegas Grand Prix when the Red Bull driver, slightly cheekily, snatched track position from his Mercedes rival as they both prepared for push laps. Irked by Verstappen's actions, which he later said he felt breached a gentleman's agreement the drivers share, Russell attempted to reclaim track position from the weaving Red Bull, with the pair making slight contact. Jamie Carragher believes Chelsea must sign a dominant centre-back or they will have "no chance of achieving anything". Chelsea have conceded 20 goals in 11 Premier League games this season and were thrashed 4-1 at home to Leeds on Saturday, which has put pressure on new manager Xabi Alonso, with his side sitting eighth and already 12 points behind leaders Arsenal. Leeds overpowered Chelsea with their physicality, as Dominic Calvert-Lewin bullied centre-backs Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana, exposing their weak defence the same way Sunderland's Brian Brobbey did in their 1-0 win before the international break. The bid was unopposed after FIFA declared it the sole valid bid in April 2025 and ratified it at an Extraordinary FIFA Congress meeting on Monday. It will be the first time the nation has hosted a football World Cup since the men's World Cup in 1966.
